title: Call It Wall Street’s Turkey of a Trading Day
summary: Cboe Global Markets, a leading provider of market infrastructure and tradable products, delivers cutting-edge trading, clearing and investment solutions to market participants around the world.
body_markdown:
*JJ Kinahan is Senior Vice President, Head of Retail Expansion and Alternative Investment Products at Cboe Global Markets, Inc. (Cboe).*


**Key Takeaways:**


- **Dip buyers step in**
- **Inflation likely fuels Fed rate hike**
- **Volatility is still high**


Whoa! What a ride. We thought the market might repeat last Friday’s selloff but dip buyers eventually stepped in and helped pull stocks off their deep morning lows. Crazy things can happen when traders take days off and it’s one of those days.


Nvidia again was a major piece of the brutal early selloff on the Nasdaq Composite, which had dropped as much as 4.7% in intraday trading. The Nasdaq 100 Index touched bear-market territory temporarily. When the bell rang, the Nasdaq Composite was off 0.62% and the Nasdaq 100 gave back 0.64%. The S&P 500 Index slumped as much as 3.21%, sinking below 7,000 before substantially trimming losses to close off at 0.35%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was battered early on as well but clawed its way back into positive territory around midday, closing higher by 0.33%.


Nvidia finished lower by 3.9%, as did a number of other technology stocks. Anthropic took an early hit too, tumbling nearly 10% from Tuesday’s close that briefly pushed its market capitalization below $1 trillion. However, it appears dip buyers jumped in and Anthropic ended the day higher by 1.08%.


There were plenty of drivers pressuring the market beyond Nvidia. Hotter-than-expected inflation data and renewed tariff concerns added to the selloff, while moves into defensive areas helped limit losses. No surprises here: the 10-year Treasury yield fell to 4.85% as investors rotated into government bonds for safety.


If anyone thinks volatility has gone away, they weren’t paying attention. Volatility climbed in early trading, but cooled somewhat as the market selloff moderated. At the close, the Cboe Volatility Index® (the VIX® Index) was just above 28, suggesting investors remained on edge about the potential for sizable market swings. Options pricing suggested an implied daily move of approximately 1.8% in the S&P 500 Index.


The Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) Price Index gave the Federal Reserve more fuel to keep interest rates higher. The Fed's preferred inflation measure, core PCE, rose 3.3% year-over-year, up from 3.1% in September and well above the Fed's 2% inflation target. Headline PCE increased 3.8%.


A December rate hike of 25 basis points has been on the table and reflected in the CME FedWatch tool for some time, but the bigger question is how far the Fed might go beyond that. The CME FedWatch tool is showing a 59% probability of another 25-basis-point increase in January, notably below the 70% probability priced in a week ago.


In other action today, S&P Global Ratings may have voiced what some investors have been thinking when it put Nvidia’s senior unsecured debt on CreditWatch with negative implications, according to a press release. The rating agency questioned the “effectiveness” of the chipmaker’s management and governance (M&G), citing board independence and “key man” risk. “At this time, S&P Global Ratings is unaware of any remedial action enacted by the board to address what could be meaningful M&G deficiencies,” the release stated.


CreditWatch does not mean the debt has been downgraded, but it is on review for one. Last week, Moody’s Ratings took a similar move, lowering Nvidia’s credit-rating outlook from positive to stable. Like S&P Global, the change was more about governance and a lack of a formal succession plan. These moves matter because they’re another piece of Nvidia’s AI involvement and could ultimately influence how the company continues with its circular financing moves.


This is another piece of the Nvidia story worth watching. The company has invested in and provided financial support to a number of other firms in the artificial intelligence (AI) ecosystem. Greater scrutiny of management oversight could eventually influence those types of investments and relationships with other AI companies.


Beware of the market on Friday. Trading volume during the half-day session tends to be extremely thin, which can make some moves look more dramatic than they really are. With fewer participants in the market, relatively small orders can have an outsized impact, leading to exaggerated swings that may reverse once more traders return to their desks on Monday. Given today’s market mayhem, some senior traders stick around for the first hour, but you can bet they’ll be gone soon after — at least based on my experience!


I’ll be off tomorrow and Friday, but back to business Monday. Have a very safe and happy Thanksgiving.


Happy Trading!
